import { distanceBetween } from 'geofire-common';
import { PRESENCE_TTL_MS } from './constants';

/** A presence doc that came back from the geohash-bounds candidate query. */
export interface Candidate {
  uid: string;
  lat: number;
  lng: number;
  /** Presence heartbeat time (`updatedAt`), epoch milliseconds. */
  updatedAtMs: number;
}

/** One selected recipient of a message. */
export interface Recipient {
  uid: string;
  /** How far the recipient was from the send location, rounded to whole metres. */
  distanceM: number;
  /** True on the sender's own copy. */
  isOwn: boolean;
}

/**
 * Selects the audience of a message from geohash-query candidates:
 * haversine distance <= radiusM AND fresh (updatedAtMs >= nowMs - PRESENCE_TTL_MS).
 *
 * The sender is ALWAYS included (distanceM 0, isOwn true) even if absent
 * from `candidates` or stale — senders receive their own messages
 * (DESIGN.md §1.5, §4 step 5).
 *
 * @param candidates candidate presences (geohash bounds give false positives)
 * @param center send location as [lat, lng]
 * @param radiusM delivery radius in metres
 * @param nowMs send time, epoch milliseconds
 * @param senderUid the authenticated sender's uid
 */
export function selectRecipients(
  candidates: readonly Candidate[],
  center: [number, number],
  radiusM: number,
  nowMs: number,
  senderUid: string,
): Recipient[] {
  const recipients: Recipient[] = [{ uid: senderUid, distanceM: 0, isOwn: true }];
  const freshnessCutoffMs = nowMs - PRESENCE_TTL_MS;

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (candidate.uid === senderUid) {
      continue; // already included above, unconditionally
    }
    if (candidate.updatedAtMs < freshnessCutoffMs) {
      continue; // stale: "not there" as far as the system is concerned
    }
    const distanceM =
      distanceBetween([candidate.lat, candidate.lng], center) * 1000;
    if (distanceM > radiusM) {
      continue; // geohash-bound false positive outside the circle
    }
    recipients.push({
      uid: candidate.uid,
      distanceM: Math.round(distanceM),
      isOwn: false,
    });
  }

  return recipients;
}

A hyperlocal messaging app. When you send a message, it is delivered to exactly
the people who were physically near you at the moment you sent it — a
**whisper** reaches 150 m, a **shout** reaches 1,500 m — and never to anyone
who arrives later. Every recipient keeps a durable personal feed of everything
they received, even while the app was in their pocket.

The full design (data model, fan-out architecture, security rules, threat
model) is in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md). The UI's
dependency-injection architecture is
[docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE.md); the dev/prod
environment plan is [docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md](docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md).

## Repository layout

```
app/                    Flutter client (ports/adapters — see docs/UI-ARCHITECTURE.md)
firebase/               Firebase project root (everything the Firebase CLI reads)
  firebase.json         Firebase project config
  .firebaserc           project aliases (committed default = dev, always)
  firestore.rules       Firestore security rules
  firestore.indexes.json  Firestore indexes (empty — single-field indexes suffice)
  functions/            Cloud Functions (TypeScript, Node 22)
dev/requirements/       executable UI requirements: spec, cases, goldens, runners
docs/                   design, UI architecture, environments
```

## Prerequisites

- Flutter SDK (stable channel)
- Node 22
- [Firebase CLI](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cli) (`npm install -g firebase-tools`)
- A Firebase project on the **Blaze** plan (required for Cloud Functions)
- [FlutterFire CLI](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/cli/) (`dart pub global activate flutterfire_cli`)

## Firebase setup

Everything below targets the **dev** project — the committed default in
`.firebaserc`. Production doesn't exist yet and nothing in this repo will
ever point at it by accident; the plan for the split (and why only

2. **Enable Google sign-in**: in the console, Authentication → Sign-in

// `selectRecipients` seeds its list with the sender unconditionally
// (`distanceM: 0`, `isOwn: true`) before it looks at a single candidate, so the
// count `sendMessage` reports back — and stores on the message doc — is
// `recipients.length - 1`. The seed and the offset are ONE fact written in two
// files that cannot see each other: drop the seed and keep the `- 1` and every
// send under-reports by one; keep the seed and drop the `- 1` and every send
// claims one recipient it never had. Neither compiles wrong, neither reddens a
// test that does not already assert the pair.
//
// Both halves are static signatures — an array initializer and an arithmetic
// expression — so the pair converts to a check. What stays prose is WHY the
// sender is unconditional (DESIGN.md §1.5: the sender's own copy must not
// depend on their presence doc existing or being fresh).
//
// Detection parses rather than greps: it reads the initializer of the
// `recipients` list inside recipients.ts and the expression bound to
// `recipientCount` in the Cloud Functions source, so `recipientCount` appearing
// in a doc comment, a response type, or an object shorthand is not a match.
//
// Dependency-free by design (a local pack's checks must load without the shared
// mount): it builds plain finding objects instead of importing the engine helper.

const SELECT_FILE = 'firebase/functions/src/recipients.ts';
const TS_ROOT = 'firebase/functions/src/';

// `const recipients: Recipient[] = [{ uid: senderUid, distanceM: 0, isOwn: true }];`
// — the initializer only, not the pushes that follow it in the candidate loop.
const SEED = /\bconst\s+recipients\s*(?::[^=]+)?=\s*(\[[^\]]*\])\s*;/;
// `const recipientCount = recipients.length - 1;` — an expression BOUND to the
// name, so `recipientCount: number` in a comment or `recipientCount,` shorthand
// in an object literal is skipped.
const COUNT = /\brecipientCount\s*[=:]\s*([^;,\n)]+)/g;
// `<something>.length` optionally followed by `- <n>`.
const LENGTH_OFFSET = /\.length\s*(?:-\s*(\d+))?/;

const rule = {
  id: 'shouts-and-whispers/sender-count-offset',
  severity: 'blocking',
  description: 'The sender seeded into selectRecipients and the offset recipientCount subtracts stay in step',
  doc: '.claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers/RULES.md',
  why: 'the sender is a recipient unconditionally (DESIGN.md §1.5), so the count reported to the sender is the list length minus exactly that seed — change one half without the other and every send reports a recipient count that is quietly wrong by one',

  run(ctx) {
    const out = [];
    const say = (file, line, what, fix) => out.push({
      rule: rule.id, severity: rule.severity, file, line,
      what, why: rule.why, fix, doc: rule.doc,
    });

    const selectText = ctx.read(SELECT_FILE);

    // Staleness guard, the idiom the pack's other checks already use: a guard
    // that quietly stops finding its subject is worse than no guard.
    if (selectText === null) {
      say(SELECT_FILE, null,
        `the sender/count guard cannot read ${SELECT_FILE}`,
        'restore the file, or point the guard at its new home (the paths live at the top of the pack\'s sender-count-offset.mjs)');
      return out;
    }

    const seedMatch = SEED.exec(selectText);
    if (!seedMatch) {
      say(SELECT_FILE, lineOf(selectText, selectText.indexOf('selectRecipients')),
        'no `recipients` list initializer found in selectRecipients — the sender/count guard has nothing to compare',
        'keep the recipient list seeded by a literal initializer at the top of selectRecipients, or point the guard at its new home');
      return out;
    }
    const seeded = /senderUid/.test(seedMatch[1]);

    const counts = countSites(ctx);
    if (!counts.length) {
      say(`${TS_ROOT}index.ts`, null,
        `no recipientCount derived from a list length found under ${TS_ROOT} — the sender/count guard has nothing to compare`,
        'keep recipientCount an explicit expression over the selectRecipients result, or point the guard at its new home');
      return out;
    }

    for (const site of counts) {
      // The offset must cancel the seed exactly: seeded → minus one, and an
      // unseeded list → no subtraction at all.
      const expected = seeded ? 1 : 0;
      if (site.offset === expected) continue;
      say(site.file, site.line,
        seeded
          ? `selectRecipients seeds the sender into the list (${SELECT_FILE}:${lineOf(selectText, seedMatch.index)}) but recipientCount subtracts ${site.offset} — it reports ${site.offset === 0 ? 'the sender as one of their own recipients' : 'the wrong count'}`

  },

// Every expression bound to `recipientCount` that is derived from a list length.
// Bindings that are not (a documented response type, a shorthand re-export) are
// not what this rule is about and are skipped.
function countSites(ctx) {
  const found = [];
  for (const file of ctx.files.filter((f) => f.startsWith(TS_ROOT) && f.endsWith('.ts'))) {
    const text = ctx.read(file);
    if (text === null) continue;
    COUNT.lastIndex = 0;
    let m;
    while ((m = COUNT.exec(text)) !== null) {
      const offset = LENGTH_OFFSET.exec(m[1]);
      if (!offset) continue;
      found.push({
        file,
        line: lineOf(text, m.index),
        offset: offset[1] === undefined ? 0 : Number(offset[1]),
      });
    }
  }
  return found;
}

function lineOf(text, index) {
  return index < 0 ? null : text.slice(0, index).split('\n').length;
}

# Shouts & Whispers — the cross-tier delivery contract

This project's own pack: the invariants that live *between* the Flutter client and the
Cloud Functions, where neither tier's compiler, analyzer, or test suite can see them. The
platform packs already own their own halves (`flutter`, `firebase`, `node`), and
`spec-driven-product` / `executable-requirements` own the loop and the spec harness — what
is left, and what is here, is the handful of agreements that break silently: no error, no
red test, just messages delivered to nobody.

The product contract these serve is [docs/DESIGN.md](../../../../docs/DESIGN.md) §1; this
file is how to keep from breaking it by accident.

## Delivery decides the audience once, and it decides it twice over

- **A geohash bounds query is a candidate query, never an answer.** `geohashQueryBounds`
  returns cells that *cover* the circle, so false positives outside the radius are
  guaranteed, not incidental. Every candidate must survive `selectRecipients` in
  `firebase/functions/src/recipients.ts` — haversine distance ≤ radius **and** fresh —
  before it becomes a recipient. Any future change that widens, caches, or short-circuits
  the query keeps the post-filter, or the radius stops meaning anything.
- **The sender is a recipient unconditionally.** `selectRecipients` seeds the list with the
  sender (`distanceM: 0`, `isOwn: true`) before it looks at a single candidate — the
  sender's own copy does not depend on their presence doc existing or being fresh
  (DESIGN.md §1.5). `recipientCount` is therefore `recipients.length - 1`, and the two
  facts move together: change one and the count reported to the sender starts lying.
- **A stale heartbeat means absent, with no fallback.** `PRESENCE_TTL_MS` is the entire
  definition of "known to be near" (DESIGN.md §1.2). A user whose last position is older
  than the cutoff is not a recipient — never "their last known position, probably still
  right". This is the mechanism behind the documented foreground-only limitation
  (DESIGN.md §7), so a fix belongs in how presence is *reported*, not in loosening the
  cutoff at selection time.

## Two encoders, one contract

The client encodes presence geohashes with a hand-rolled encoder
(`app/lib/geo/geohash.dart`, ~30 lines, no dependency); the server encodes and range-queries
with `geofire-common`. They must produce **identical** strings, including at bisection
midpoints — both use a strict `>` comparison, which puts a coordinate exactly on a midpoint
in the lower half-cell. That agreement is what the known-vector suites on both sides exist
for (`app/test/geohash_test.dart` and `firebase/functions/test/geohash-compat.test.ts` carry
the *same* vectors deliberately); touching either encoder means re-running both, and
extending one vector list means extending the other.

The matching *precision* is mechanical and is checked (`geohash-precision-parity`); the
matching *encoding* is not, which is why it is stated here.

## One table, two copies

[docs/DESIGN.md](../../../../docs/DESIGN.md) §10 is the source of truth for every constant
both tiers carry; `firebase/functions/src/constants.ts` and `app/lib/config.dart` are
transcriptions of it, kept honest by the `cross-tier-constants` check. Adding a cross-tier
constant is a four-part change: the §10 row, the server copy, the client copy, and the
`PAIRS` map in the check — a value absent from `PAIRS` is a value nothing is guarding. A
constant only one tier needs (the send cooldown, the heartbeat cadence) stays out of `PAIRS`
on purpose: it cannot drift, because there is nothing to drift from.

## Running the pack's checks

```sh
node --test .claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers/pack.test.mjs
```

# shouts-and-whispers pack (local)

This repo's own pack: the **cross-tier delivery contract** between the Flutter client
(`app/`) and the Cloud Functions (`firebase/functions/`) — the agreements neither tier's
compiler, analyzer, or test suite can see, and that fail silently when broken (no error, no
red test, just messages delivered to nobody).

Declared by hand as `local/shouts-and-whispers` in `.claudinite-checks.json`; never
fingerprinted (`detect`/`marker` are null). It deliberately holds nothing the canon already
homes: `flutter`, `firebase`, `node`, `android`, `ios` own their platforms,
`spec-driven-product` and `executable-requirements` own the loop and the spec harness.

## Checks

| Rule (≤5 words) | Severity | What |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-tier constants agree | blocking | the constants both tiers carry hold the same value, and match `docs/DESIGN.md` §10 |
| Geohash precision matches | blocking | client heartbeat and `sendMessage` encode presence geohashes at the same precision |

Both carry a staleness guard: if a guarded declaration or call site is renamed or moved out
of the scanned tree, the check says so instead of quietly passing.

`cross-tier-constants` is deliberately *not* the canon `shared-constants` guard: that one
byte-counts a declared literal per file, which here collides on substrings (`150` inside
`1500`), cannot express the paired identifiers (`WHISPER_RADIUS_M` / `whisperRadiusM`), and
only covers values someone remembered to declare. Pairing by name needs no per-value upkeep.

## Prose (`RULES.md`) — by section

| Section (≤5 words) | How enforced |
|---|---|
| Delivery decides the audience twice | prose (candidate query + post-filter, sender always included, stale means absent) |
| Two encoders, one contract | prose + the `geohash-precision-parity` check (+ both tiers' known-vector suites) |
| One table, two copies | prose + the `cross-tier-constants` check |

## Fixtures

```sh
node --test .claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers/pack.test.mjs
```

Nine cases: each check red on a violating fixture, quiet on a clean one, red on its
staleness case, and quiet when run against the real repo tree (so a check that stops
matching the project's actual files fails here instead of passing vacuously).

Distilled from this repo's own code and design: `docs/DESIGN.md` §1/§3/§10,
`firebase/functions/src/{constants,index,recipients}.ts`, `app/lib/{config,geo/geohash}.dart`,
`app/lib/adapters/geolocator_location_adapter.dart`, and the paired known-vector suites
`app/test/geohash_test.dart` / `firebase/functions/test/geohash-compat.test.ts`.

function serverValue(text, name) {
  const m = new RegExp(`^export const ${name}\\s*=\\s*([^;]+);`, 'm').exec(text);
  return m ? normalize(m[1]) : null;
}

// `const int name = <value>;` / `const String name = '<value>';` — config.dart's shape.
function clientValue(text, name) {
  const m = new RegExp(`^const\\s+\\w+\\s+${name}\\s*=\\s*([^;]+);`, 'm').exec(text);
  return m ? normalize(m[1]) : null;
}

function designValue(text, name) {
  if (text === null) return null;
  const m = new RegExp(`^\\|\\s*\`${name}\`\\s*\\|([^|]*)\\|`, 'm').exec(text);
  return m ? normalize(m[1]) : null;
}

// Compare values, not spelling: strip whitespace and one layer of quotes so
// 'us-central1' and "us-central1" are the same value.
function normalize(raw) {
  const v = raw.trim();
  const quoted = /^(['"])(.*)\1$/.exec(v);
  return quoted ? quoted[2] : v;

import { distanceBetween } from 'geofire-common';
import { PRESENCE_TTL_MS } from './constants';

/** A presence doc that came back from the geohash-bounds candidate query. */
export interface Candidate {
  uid: string;
  lat: number;
  lng: number;
  /** Presence heartbeat time (`updatedAt`), epoch milliseconds. */
  updatedAtMs: number;
}

/** One selected recipient of a message. */
export interface Recipient {
  uid: string;
  /** How far the recipient was from the send location, rounded to whole metres. */
  distanceM: number;
  /** True on the sender's own copy. */
  isOwn: boolean;
}

/**
 * Selects the audience of a message from geohash-query candidates:
 * haversine distance <= radiusM AND fresh (updatedAtMs >= nowMs - PRESENCE_TTL_MS).
 *
 * The sender is ALWAYS included (distanceM 0, isOwn true) even if absent
 * from `candidates` or stale — senders receive their own messages
 * (DESIGN.md §1.5, §4 step 5).
 *
 * @param candidates candidate presences (geohash bounds give false positives)
 * @param center send location as [lat, lng]
 * @param radiusM delivery radius in metres
 * @param nowMs send time, epoch milliseconds
 * @param senderUid the authenticated sender's uid
 */
export function selectRecipients(
  candidates: readonly Candidate[],
  center: [number, number],
  radiusM: number,
  nowMs: number,
  senderUid: string,
): Recipient[] {
  const recipients: Recipient[] = [{ uid: senderUid, distanceM: 0, isOwn: true }];
  const freshnessCutoffMs = nowMs - PRESENCE_TTL_MS;

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    if (candidate.uid === senderUid) {
      continue; // already included above, unconditionally
    }
    if (candidate.updatedAtMs < freshnessCutoffMs) {
      continue; // stale: "not there" as far as the system is concerned
    }
    const distanceM =
      distanceBetween([candidate.lat, candidate.lng], center) * 1000;
    if (distanceM > radiusM) {
      continue; // geohash-bound false positive outside the circle
    }
    recipients.push({
      uid: candidate.uid,
      distanceM: Math.round(distanceM),
      isOwn: false,
    });
  }

  return recipients;
}

// files that cannot see each other: drop the seed and keep the `- 1` and every
// send under-reports by one; keep the seed and drop the `- 1` and every send
// claims one recipient it never had. Neither compiles wrong, neither reddens a
// test that does not already assert the pair.
//
// Both halves are static signatures — an array initializer and an arithmetic
// expression — so the pair converts to a check. What stays prose is WHY the
// sender is unconditional (DESIGN.md §1.5: the sender's own copy must not
// depend on their presence doc existing or being fresh).
//
// Detection parses rather than greps: it reads the initializer of the
// `recipients` list inside recipients.ts and the expression bound to
// `recipientCount` in the Cloud Functions source, so `recipientCount` appearing
// in a doc comment, a response type, or an object shorthand is not a match.
//
// Dependency-free by design (a local pack's checks must load without the shared
// mount): it builds plain finding objects instead of importing the engine helper.

const SELECT_FILE = 'firebase/functions/src/recipients.ts';
const TS_ROOT = 'firebase/functions/src/';

// — the initializer only, not the pushes that follow it in the candidate loop.
const SEED = /\bconst\s+recipients\s*(?::[^=]+)?=\s*(\[[^\]]*\])\s*;/;
// `const recipientCount = recipients.length - 1;` — an expression BOUND to the
// name, so `recipientCount: number` in a comment or `recipientCount,` shorthand
// in an object literal is skipped.
const COUNT = /\brecipientCount\s*[=:]\s*([^;,\n)]+)/g;
// `<something>.length` optionally followed by `- <n>`.
const LENGTH_OFFSET = /\.length\s*(?:-\s*(\d+))?/;

const rule = {
  id: 'shouts-and-whispers/sender-count-offset',
  severity: 'blocking',
  description: 'The sender seeded into selectRecipients and the offset recipientCount subtracts stay in step',
  doc: '.claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers/RULES.md',
  why: 'the sender is a recipient unconditionally (DESIGN.md §1.5), so the count reported to the sender is the list length minus exactly that seed — change one half without the other and every send reports a recipient count that is quietly wrong by one',

    const out = [];
    const say = (file, line, what, fix) => out.push({
      rule: rule.id, severity: rule.severity, file, line,
      what, why: rule.why, fix, doc: rule.doc,
    });

    const selectText = ctx.read(SELECT_FILE);

    // Staleness guard, the idiom the pack's other checks already use: a guard
    // that quietly stops finding its subject is worse than no guard.
    if (selectText === null) {
      say(SELECT_FILE, null,
        `the sender/count guard cannot read ${SELECT_FILE}`,
        'restore the file, or point the guard at its new home (the paths live at the top of the pack\'s sender-count-offset.mjs)');
      return out;
    }

    const seedMatch = SEED.exec(selectText);
    if (!seedMatch) {
      say(SELECT_FILE, lineOf(selectText, selectText.indexOf('selectRecipients')),
        'no `recipients` list initializer found in selectRecipients — the sender/count guard has nothing to compare',
        'keep the recipient list seeded by a literal initializer at the top of selectRecipients, or point the guard at its new home');
      return out;
    }
    const seeded = /senderUid/.test(seedMatch[1]);

    const counts = countSites(ctx);
    if (!counts.length) {
      say(`${TS_ROOT}index.ts`, null,
        `no recipientCount derived from a list length found under ${TS_ROOT} — the sender/count guard has nothing to compare`,
        'keep recipientCount an explicit expression over the selectRecipients result, or point the guard at its new home');
      return out;
    }

    for (const site of counts) {
      // The offset must cancel the seed exactly: seeded → minus one, and an
      // unseeded list → no subtraction at all.
      const expected = seeded ? 1 : 0;
      if (site.offset === expected) continue;
      say(site.file, site.line,
        seeded

  },

// Every expression bound to `recipientCount` that is derived from a list length.
// Bindings that are not (a documented response type, a shorthand re-export) are
// not what this rule is about and are skipped.
function countSites(ctx) {
  const found = [];
  for (const file of ctx.files.filter((f) => f.startsWith(TS_ROOT) && f.endsWith('.ts'))) {
    const text = ctx.read(file);
    if (text === null) continue;

    let m;

      const offset = LENGTH_OFFSET.exec(m[1]);
      if (!offset) continue;
      found.push({
        file,
        line: lineOf(text, m.index),
        offset: offset[1] === undefined ? 0 : Number(offset[1]),
      });
    }
  }
  return found;
}

  return index < 0 ? null : text.slice(0, index).split('\n').length;
}

const RECIPIENTS_TS = (seed) => `
export function selectRecipients(candidates, center, radiusM, nowMs, senderUid) {
  const recipients: Recipient[] = ${seed};
  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    recipients.push({ uid: candidate.uid, distanceM: 0, isOwn: false });
  }
  return recipients;
}
`;
const SEEDED = '[{ uid: senderUid, distanceM: 0, isOwn: true }]';

const INDEX_TS = (countExpr) => `
/** Response: { messageId: string, recipientCount: number } (count excludes sender) */
const recipients = selectRecipients(candidates, [lat, lng], radiusM, nowMs, uid);
const recipientCount = ${countExpr};
await messageRef.set({ text, recipientCount });
return { messageId: messageRef.id, recipientCount };
`;

const senderFiles = (seed, countExpr) => ({
  'firebase/functions/src/recipients.ts': RECIPIENTS_TS(seed),
  'firebase/functions/src/index.ts': INDEX_TS(countExpr),

test('sender-count-offset: fires when the sender seed goes away but the offset stays', () => {
  const findings = senderCountOffset.run(ctxOf(senderFiles('[]', 'recipients.length - 1')));
  assert.equal(findings.length, 1);
  assert.match(findings[0].what, /no longer seeds the sender into the list/);

test('sender-count-offset: quiet when neither seeds nor subtracts', () => {

One conversion from the `prose-to-checks-sweep` run of 2026-07-28 over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the binding scope). Logged on the tracker, #22.

## The prose

`RULES.md` §"Two encoders, one contract" carried an always-testable half as prose:

> the known-vector suites on both sides ... carry the *same* vectors deliberately; touching either encoder means re-running both, **and extending one vector list means extending the other**.

Nothing enforced that last clause. Add a vector to `app/test/geohash_test.dart` and not to `firebase/functions/test/geohash-compat.test.ts` (or the reverse) and **both suites stay green** — different languages, different runners, different CI jobs — while the compatibility claim silently stops covering that coordinate. The two encoders only meet in those two files, and the two files never meet at all.

## Why this one is a check and not a test in disguise

It asserts nothing about what either encoder *does*. It compares two committed tables of literals that must agree — the same static-signature shape as this pack's existing `cross-tier-constants` guard, which pairs declarations across two files that cannot share an import. The encoders' *behavioural* agreement stays prose, because no post-hoc scan can run one encoder against the other; that is precisely what the suites themselves are for.

## The check

`shouts-and-whispers/geohash-vector-parity` (blocking). It **parses rather than greps**: only assertions written at the shared production precision 9 are read — the client's default-precision `encode(lat, lng)` calls and the server's explicit `geohashForLocation([lat, lng], 9)` calls — so the deliberately unpaired cases (the client's precision 1/5/11/12 vectors, the server's 10-char default-precision ones) are never mistaken for drift. Coordinates compare as numbers, not spelling.

It fires when:
- either suite carries a precision-9 coordinate the other lacks (both directions),
- the two suites expect **different** hashes for the same coordinate,
- a suite is unreadable or stops carrying precision-9 vectors at all (the staleness guard this pack's other checks also carry — a guard that quietly stops guarding is worse than none).

## See-it-fail

Mandatory and done twice over. Seven fixtures in `pack.test.mjs` (fixtures 9 → 16, all passing), **and** additionally verified red against mutations of the *real* suites — a client-only vector, a server-only vector, and a one-character hash drift each produce exactly one finding; the unmutated tree is quiet.

## Prose trimmed

The §"Two encoders, one contract" enforcement clause is now rationale only: why a one-sided vector is invisible, and why the encoding agreement itself cannot be scanned. The pack `README.md` tables and fixture count are updated to match.

## Scope

Confined to `.claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers` — one new module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixtures, and the trimmed prose. Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` (the read-only mounted canon) is touched, and no rule an existing check already covers was re-converted.

Offline suite green: `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers/pack.test.mjs` 16/16, `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both clean.

Swept `.claudinite/local/packs` (binding scope) — one local pack, `shouts-and-whispers`.

**Prose converted:** `RULES.md` §"Two encoders, one contract" — *"extending one vector list means extending the other"* → check `shouts-and-whispers/geohash-vector-parity` (blocking), PR #35.

The two known-vector suites (`app/test/geohash_test.dart`, `firebase/functions/test/geohash-compat.test.ts`) carry the same vectors deliberately, and that overlap is the only evidence the hand-rolled Dart encoder and geofire-common agree. Add a vector to one suite alone and both stay green — different languages, different runners, different CI jobs — while the compatibility claim quietly stops covering that coordinate. Two committed tables of literals that must agree: the same static-signature shape as the pack's accepted `cross-tier-constants` guard, asserting nothing about what either encoder *does*. The check parses rather than greps — only precision-9 assertions (the client's default-precision `encode`, the server's explicit `geohashForLocation([lat, lng], 9)`), so the deliberately unpaired cases (client precision 1/5/11/12, server 10-char default) are not mistaken for drift. See-it-fail proven in all three directions (client-only vector, server-only vector, hash drift) plus two staleness cases, on fixtures **and** against mutations of the real suites; quiet clean and on the real tree. Pack fixtures 9 → 16, all passing; `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` clean.

**Heeded from the 2026-07-27 follow-up above:** the sender-seed / `recipientCount` arithmetic rule was *not* re-attempted. It was independently re-derived as this run's first candidate and built out before the tracker thread was read; on finding the owner's rejection it was reverted in full (working tree returned to HEAD, original 9 fixtures re-run green) before any of it reached a branch. Nothing from that attempt is in PR #35. That rule stays prose.

**Left as prose (deliberately, not a backlog):**
- The encoders' *character-for-character* agreement, same section — no post-hoc scan can run one encoder against the other; that is what the suites exist for. The prose now says so as its rationale.
- *"A geohash bounds query is a candidate query, never an answer"* and *"A stale heartbeat means absent, with no fallback"* — runtime behaviour, not static signatures; covered where it counts by `firebase/functions/test/recipients.test.ts`. Unchanged judgement from the 2026-07-27 run.
- *"The sender is a recipient unconditionally"* — per the rejection above.
- §"One table, two copies" — already the `cross-tier-constants` check.

Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` was touched, and no rule an existing check already covers was re-converted.

{"number":35,"title":"Prose to checks: pair the two tiers' geohash known-vector suites","body":"One conversion from the `prose-to-checks-sweep` run of 2026-07-28 over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the binding scope). Logged on the tracker, #22.

## The prose

`RULES.md` §"Two encoders, one contract" carried an always-testable half as prose:

> the known-vector suites on both sides ... carry the *same* vectors deliberately; touching either encoder means re-running both, **and extending one vector list means extending the other**.

Nothing enforced that last clause. Add a vector to `app/test/geohash_test.dart` and not to `firebase/functions/test/geohash-compat.test.ts` (or the reverse) and **both suites stay green** — different languages, different runners, different CI jobs — while the compatibility claim silently stops covering that coordinate. The two encoders only meet in those two files, and the two files never meet at all.

## Why this one is a check and not a test in disguise

It asserts nothing about what either encoder *does*. It compares two committed tables of literals that must agree — the same static-signature shape as this pack's existing `cross-tier-constants` guard, which pairs declarations across two files that cannot share an import. The encoders' *behavioural* agreement stays prose, because no post-hoc scan can run one encoder against the other; that is precisely what the suites themselves are for.

## The check

`shouts-and-whispers/geohash-vector-parity` (blocking). It **parses rather than greps**: only assertions written at the shared production precision 9 are read — the client's default-precision `encode(lat, lng)` calls and the server's explicit `geohashForLocation([lat, lng], 9)` calls — so the deliberately unpaired cases (the client's precision 1/5/11/12 vectors, the server's 10-char default-precision ones) are never mistaken for drift. Coordinates compare as numbers, not spelling.

It fires when:
- either suite carries a precision-9 coordinate the other lacks (both directions),
- the two suites expect **different** hashes for the same coordinate,
- a suite is unreadable or stops carrying precision-9 vectors at all (the staleness guard this pack's other checks also carry — a guard that quietly stops guarding is worse than none).

## See-it-fail

Mandatory and done twice over. Seven fixtures in `pack.test.mjs` (fixtures 9 → 16, all passing), **and** additionally verified red against mutations of the *real* suites — a client-only vector, a server-only vector, and a one-character hash drift each produce exactly one finding; the unmutated tree is quiet.

## Prose trimmed

The §"Two encoders, one contract" enforcement clause is now rationale only: why a one-sided vector is invisible, and why the encoding agreement itself cannot be scanned. The pack `README.md` tables and fixture count are updated to match.

## Scope

Confined to `.claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers` — one new module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixtures, and the trimmed prose. Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` (the read-only mounted canon) is touched, and no rule an existing check already covers was re-converted.

Offline suite green: `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers/pack.test.mjs` 16/16, `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both clean.

[{"number":35,"title":"Prose to checks: pair the two tiers' geohash known-vector suites","body":"One conversion from the `prose-to-checks-sweep` run of 2026-07-28 over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the binding scope). Logged on the tracker, #22.

## The prose

`RULES.md` §"Two encoders, one contract" carried an always-testable half as prose:

> the known-vector suites on both sides ... carry the *same* vectors deliberately; touching either encoder means re-running both, **and extending one vector list means extending the other**.

Nothing enforced that last clause. Add a vector to `app/test/geohash_test.dart` and not to `firebase/functions/test/geohash-compat.test.ts` (or the reverse) and **both suites stay green** — different languages, different runners, different CI jobs — while the compatibility claim silently stops covering that coordinate. The two encoders only meet in those two files, and the two files never meet at all.

## Why this one is a check and not a test in disguise

It asserts nothing about what either encoder *does*. It compares two committed tables of literals that must agree — the same static-signature shape as this pack's existing `cross-tier-constants` guard, which pairs declarations across two files that cannot share an import. The encoders' *behavioural* agreement stays prose, because no post-hoc scan can run one encoder against the other; that is precisely what the suites themselves are for.

## The check

`shouts-and-whispers/geohash-vector-parity` (blocking). It **parses rather than greps**: only assertions written at the shared production precision 9 are read — the client's default-precision `encode(lat, lng)` calls and the server's explicit `geohashForLocation([lat, lng], 9)` calls — so the deliberately unpaired cases (the client's precision 1/5/11/12 vectors, the server's 10-char default-precision ones) are never mistaken for drift. Coordinates compare as numbers, not spelling.

It fires when:
- either suite carries a precision-9 coordinate the other lacks (both directions),
- the two suites expect **different** hashes for the same coordinate,
- a suite is unreadable or stops carrying precision-9 vectors at all (the staleness guard this pack's other checks also carry — a guard that quietly stops guarding is worse than none).

## See-it-fail

Mandatory and done twice over. Seven fixtures in `pack.test.mjs` (fixtures 9 → 16, all passing), **and** additionally verified red against mutations of the *real* suites — a client-only vector, a server-only vector, and a one-character hash drift each produce exactly one finding; the unmutated tree is quiet.

## Prose trimmed

The §"Two encoders, one contract" enforcement clause is now rationale only: why a one-sided vector is invisible, and why the encoding agreement itself cannot be scanned. The pack `README.md` tables and fixture count are updated to match.

## Scope

Confined to `.claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers` — one new module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixtures, and the trimmed prose. Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` (the read-only mounted canon) is touched, and no rule an existing check already covers was re-converted.

Offline suite green: `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/shouts-and-whispers/pack.test.mjs` 16/16, `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both clean.

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.

4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.
